questions.question: A 52-year-old woman presents with a thunderclap headache. CT angiography is shown. Which is the most common location of intracranial saccular aneurysms?
questions.explanation: The **anterior communicating artery** complex is the most frequent site (~30-35%), followed by the PComm origin and the MCA bifurcation. About 85-95% of saccular aneurysms arise in the anterior circulation.

questions.question: A 4 cm AVM is located in the left motor cortex and drains only into superficial cortical veins. What is its Spetzler-Martin grade?
questions.explanation:
Size 3-6 cm = 2 points, eloquent location = 1, superficial drainage only = 0. Total **grade III**.

| Feature | Points |
|---|---|
| Size < 3 cm / 3-6 cm / > 6 cm | 1 / 2 / 3 |
| Eloquent cortex | 0 / 1 |
| Deep venous drainage | 0 / 1 |

questions.question: A patient with aneurysmal SAH is drowsy and confused with a mild focal deficit. What is the Hunt and Hess grade?
questions.explanation: Hunt and Hess: 1 asymptomatic/mild headache; 2 moderate-severe headache, nuchal rigidity, cranial nerve palsy only; **3 drowsiness, confusion or mild focal deficit**; 4 stupor, moderate-severe hemiparesis; 5 deep coma, decerebrate posturing.
